articles.body: Earlier this year, the Kansas City Current brought its community-focused mission closer to home, creating new opportunities for young soccer players and earning recognition for Brittany Mahomes' leadership. The club, co-owned by Brittany and Patrick Mahomes, announced a free youth soccer league in Kansas City's historic Northeast neighbourhood. The initiative aimed to remove financial barriers for children eager to play, while Brittany's work with the Current also earned her a notable honour celebrating women's leadership and progress in sports.Kansas City Current's free soccer league opens doors for young playersThe 9th & Van Brunt Soccer League was designed to give children an opportunity to experience the game without the cost often tied to organised sports. Set to begin on July 11, the programme targeted children aged 8 to 10, with organisers expecting around 120 participants during the summer.For families in the Northeast neighbourhood, the league offered more than a chance to play. Accessible youth sports can help children build confidence, learn teamwork and form connections with peers. By removing participation costs, the Current aimed to make those experiences available to more young people.Kansas City Current President Raven Jemison highlighted the wider purpose behind the initiative in a statement.“Launching the 9th & Van Brunt Soccer League is a perfect embodiment of the Kansas City Current’s community pillars. We could not be more appreciative of our incredible partners and staff that helped bring this to life,”Jemison also pointed to the programme's potential to create lasting connections across the city.“This league will have a generational impact on young athletes, families and coaches across the city. We are excited to see how the league grows and the success stories that come from it.”Brittany Mahomes, a former professional soccer player and founding co-owner of the Current, showed her support by liking the announcement on Instagram and sharing it on her Stories. Patrick Mahomes' mother, Randi, also welcomed the news, commenting, “So amazing 🤍.”Brittany Mahomes receives recognition for women's sports leadershipThe youth league announcement came amid further recognition of Brittany Mahomes' work with the Current. United WE, a national women's leadership organisation, presented her with its inaugural Champion for Change Award at CPKC Stadium.Brittany Mahomes celebrated the honour on Instagram, writing:“Such an inspiring morning with @unitedwe__ celebrating progress and influencing action!“It was such an honor to receive the inaugural Champion for Change award in the stadium that represents what it looks like when women’s needs are prioritized in sports and in the workplace. No better place to celebrate women than a stadium built for women! Thank you @unitedwe__ and @wendyddoyle for the incredible honor!”Patrick celebrated his wife's achievement, commenting, “Congrats babe! You deserve it! Love you!” He also reshared her post on his Stories.United WE's statement recognised Brittany's role in the Mahomes family's philanthropic work through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which has contributed millions to initiatives supporting children's health, wellness and opportunity in underserved communities.“Through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, she and her husband, Patrick Mahomes, have contributed millions to initiatives advancing children’s health, wellness, and opportunity in underserved communities.“Her leadership demonstrates that when women are visible, invested, and at the decision-making table, communities and economies grow stronger.”Together, the league and Brittany's award underscored the Current's focus on community access, youth development and women's leadership, extending the club's influence well beyond matchday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Updated Win-Loss Predictions for Bills After Hot 2-0 Start
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills continue their quest for the NFL's first-ever 17-0 regular season when they face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at Highmark Stadium.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills continue their quest for the NFL's first-ever 17-0 regular season when they face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at Highmark Stadium.

OK, maybe we're getting a bit ahead of ourselves.

Regardless, the goal is a W every week, as Buffalo is on track through two games in 2026.

Let's look at the remaining schedule to see where Buffalo might stumble and predict how things will play out for Josh Allen and Co. between now and January.

Los Angeles comes limping into a tough road spot. Buffalo is as well, with Ed Oliver (hip) and DJ Moore (shoulder) both up in the air. Still, I can't see that defense slowing Josh Allen down. Buffalo's defense should perform well against an offense that hasn't clicked yet.

This could go either way, as New England beat Buffalo on the road in the first week of October last year and went on to win the division. That said, the Patriots have come back to earth a bit. That's realistically unlikely to happen two years in a row.

This wraps up a damn tough run of games for both teams, but the Rams are at home in prime time and are one of the few teams in the NFL with as much talent as the Bills. They win a thriller, with their receivers having a big advantage over the vulnerable Buffalo secondary.

A get-right game, as they are more acclimated to the Pacific time zone. That said, even coming off a projected loss in L.A., the Raiders are sneaky. If Buffalo upsets the Rams and enters 5-0, it becomes an even bigger trap for a tired team looking ahead to its bye.

Two weeks to prepare for a home game against an overrated rival whose number they've had in recent years? I'm not even sure this'll be close.

The Bills lay a sudden egg a couple of times per season. I sense one of those will come on this mini road trip to Minnesota and New York. Justin Jefferson could be a handful here.

Facing the talented, spunky Vikings in a prime-time road game makes more sense as an L on this roadie, but if they pull that one off, I can see the egg-laying taking place against a Jets team that knows them well and might be flying under the radar. Basically, I have them splitting their October road trip as well as this one.

Miami beat the Bills last November, but this is a very different team. Thus far, it hasn't looked like one that is NFL-caliber. This is a tough road spot for the Dolphins.

They're lucky to get the juggernaut Chiefs at home with Kansas City traveling on short rest for a Thanksgiving Thursday nighter. They win a memorable one at Highmark.

Buying or Selling Teams Going Into Week 3 📊

Tough call here. The Patriots have a later bye and could be fresher for this home game, but the Bills also benefit from extra rest following Thursday's matchup with Kansas City. If Buffalo wins this, it probably suffers an egg-laying letdown in Green Bay.

For the third time in three months, I have them going 1-1 on a mini road trip. In this case, I'll give them the victory in New England on extra rest and then have them fall to the Packers in a tough prime-time spot at Lambeau.

This is the back half of a two-game road swing for the Bears, who may lack what it takes to slow down the Buffalo offense in prime time at Highmark.

Totally winnable game for Buffalo, but few would fault them for falling in this road spot against a prime contender.

You have to wonder if this is a potential upset alert. The Dolphins could have a lot more figured out by this point. It's their second home game in a row. They did hammer the Bills at this site last November. I'll go W, but could see this being a letdown L if the Bills are coming off a win in Denver. Either way, it works out to another 1-1 road trip.

This is likely only a loss if it doesn't matter, which is unlikely considering that I've given them four road losses in October, November and December. This should be enough to recapture the AFC East crown and contend for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

articles.title: Panic Meters for Struggling NFL QBs Entering Week 3 of the 2026 Season
articles.summary: There have been some rough starts.
articles.body:
We're looking at you, Justin Herbert. And you, Aaron Rodgers. You too, Drake Maye, Cam Ward and Bo Nix. Far-from-ideal starts for each of you.

To what extent should each be panicking as we enter Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season? Let's break it down.

The Problem: The 28-year-old has already thrown three interceptions, fumbled three times and is the third-lowest-rated qualified passer in the league. His 24.4 rating on deep passes is the worst among quarterbacks with at least 10 deep attempts.

The Solution: The entire offense—and Herbert in particular—has to figure out how to effectively run and perform in new coordinator Mike McDaniel's system. They look completely out of sync and have been plagued by mental mistakes. It has to click soon because they are in Buffalo and Seattle over the next two weeks.

Panic Level: 8/10 -- Not because a talented quarterback like Herbert can't eventually figure this out, but because he's also relying on a so-so offense and facing a brutal schedule. Time is already running out for an offense that has scored 28 total points in back-to-back losses to start the season.

The Problem: The fading 42-year-old is the league's fourth-lowest-rated passer. He's just 3-for-26 on deep passes and 5-for-19 on third-down throws . The Steelers have scored 23 total points in two games.

The Solution: Strip out the playbook clutter. It won't be easy, but Rodgers and Mike McCarthy have to show that the modern game hasn't passed them by. They'll have to make major adjustments to take the pressure off Rodgers in the pocket. Either that or the organization might have to pivot in a major way.

Panic Level: 9/10 -- Rodgers and the offense can't afford another dud this weekend against Cincinnati. They're digging an early hole that will be hard to climb out of as the schedule gets tougher in November and December.

The Problem: The reigning MVP runner-up is the NFL's second-lowest-rated qualified passer. He has a 29.6 passer rating on third down and an abysmal 43.6 rating in the second half of one-score games . On deep attempts, he's thrown zero touchdown passes and four interceptions as the Patriots have scored just 30 points in two weeks.

The Solution: Facing some weaker defenses should help, as the Seahawks and Steelers bring a lot of talent to the table. Still, Josh McDaniels' offense has to become less predictable and rely less on Maye to play hero ball in big spots. Meanwhile, Maye himself simply needs to make more plays when called upon. The 24-year-old has looked lost thus far.

Panic Level: 5/10 -- It's early. They're still 1-1. Maye was at least better in a Week 2 win than he was in a Week 1 loss. That said, a few more poor performances could cause skeptics to wonder if the league has figured him out after he shocked the football world in 2025.

Buying or Selling Teams Going Into Week 3 📊

The Problem: In two weeks, the second-year No. 1 overall pick has completed two passes for 15-plus yards downfield. He's led the Titans to just 30 points in two games. More critically, he's often looked completely overwhelmed under tight reins.

The Solution: The offense has to start letting him loose. Ward has completed eight third-down passes, but only four have resulted in first downs. He also ranks fifth-lowest among qualifiers in terms of air yards per attempt. We can't get a read on whether Ward has a chance to be the real deal when he's this handcuffed.

Panic Level: 3/10 -- He's only 19 starts into his career. There were bound to be growing pains adjusting to Brian Daboll's offense. The Titans have time to tinker, as we did see progress from Ward and the offense against Philadelphia in Week 2.

The Problem: He fumbled three times in a poor Week 1 performance against the Chiefs and has thrown an interception in each of the first two weeks. The Broncos have scored just 30 points in those two games. Nix has thrown 17 passes on third down. Only four of which have moved the chains.

The Solution: Mainly patience, as we saw the new-look offense begin to click during the second half of Sunday's victory over the Jaguars. That said, consistency has been an issue for both Nix and the Denver offense in the past, so the pressure is firmly on. Nix has to find a way to be effective for four quarters, with the staff keeping him on schedule.

Panic Level: 3/10 -- This is a quality team across the board with a new play-caller. Nix has the talent and support to get by while ideally making progress as Year 3 continues. There's some margin for error here.

articles.title: Packers' Jordan Love Recaps 'Frustrating' Loss to Falcons, 'It's Back to the Drawing Board'
articles.summary: A tough start to the season for the Green Bay Packers may have hit its nadir on Thursday night with a 35-14 home loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
A tough start to the season for the Green Bay Packers may have hit its nadir on Thursday night with a 35-14 home loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

Following the 21-point defeat, Packers quarterback Jordan Love called it a "frustrating" game and "it's back to the drawing board" for the team as they look to find ways to turn things around.

If not for some poor game management by New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn in Week 2, the Packers realistically could be 0-3.

The overtime victory over the Jets gave the Packers a slight reprieve, but all of that slipped away with a loss against a previously-winless Falcons team that had not reached the red zone in their first two games.

This isn't even a situation where you can point to one thing that's not working. The Packers have been bad in almost every phase of the game thus far. Their defense held up well through the first two games before giving up 498 yards to Atlanta, including 242 on the ground.

Offensively, things have been a mess thanks to bad blocking by an injury-ravaged line and turnovers. Love leads the NFL with four fumbles (one lost) and he's been sacked eight times through three games. His current sack rate of 6.06 percent is markedly higher than his career rate of 4.4 percent.

Opposing defenses creating constant pressure is also resulting in Love completing just 52.4 percent of his pass attempts this season. Compounding matters, Green Bay can't run the ball, with a total of 146 rushing yards through three games.

For comparison, Falcons running back Bijan Robinson had more rushing yards on Thursday night (194) than the entire Packers team has this season.

Since Micah Parsons tore his ACL in Week 15 last season, the Packers are 1-7 in their last eight games, including a playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. They do get a few extra days to try and figure things out before a Week 4 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium.

articles.title: Predicting Cleveland Browns' 2026 Season Stat Leaders After 2 Weeks
articles.summary: It's only been two weeks, but we've already learned a lot about the 2026 Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
It's only been two weeks, but we've already learned a lot about the 2026 Cleveland Browns.

For one, they are capable of winning a game on the road if Deshaun Watson plays efficient football.

There's still a lot for the team to prove. There's plenty of time for those off to a rocky start to set things right. There's also time for players off to a hot start to cool off.

With that in mind, it's a good time to revisit who is going to be leading this team statistically and what their final statline could look like. Here, we'll look at some of the major statistical categories and project who will lead the way as the season starts to unfold.

2025 Leader: Shedeur Sanders (120-of-212, 1,400 yards, 7 TD, 10 INT)

It looked like an inevitability that Shedeur Sanders would be the starting quarterback for the Browns after Week 1. After Week 2, it truly seems like Watson's job to lose.

Todd Monken has been steadfast that the veteran gives them the best chance to win. He was vindicated in Week 2. The Browns upset the Bucs and Watson was efficient in the win.

He didn't really push the ball downfield. His average depth of target was just 3.6 yards, but it resulted in a statline of 24-of-30 for 238 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.

That might be the ceiling for the version of Watson that the Browns are getting at this point. It's hard to see him putting up huge numbers if he's going to play conservatively outside of a few deep shots to Denzel Boston every game.

That being said, he could put together the kind of efficient season that the Browns need to see what their skill players could do and keep Sanders on the bench.

Projected Statline: 280-of-424, 3,083 yards, 18 TD, 10 INT

2025 Leader: Quinshon Judkins (230 attempts, 827 yards and 7 TD)

The most surprising development for the Browns this season might be that the run game has been the most disappointing aspect. There was optimism that Quinshon Judkins could take the next step.

There's more to the run game than Judkins' contributions. The offensive line hasn't necessarily done its part either. But Judkins' PFF grade ranks 46th among the 60 they have graded this season.

The Browns are currently 30th in yards before contact, according to Pro Football Reference . They also have zero broken tackles.

There's a case to be made that Judkins will get better with time. Every week puts more distance between himself and the dislocated ankle and broken fibula that ended his season last year.

We'll get a better idea if Judkins can turn things around in Week 3. The Panthers gave up the most rushing yards through the first two weeks of the season.

For now, it's hard to see him really improving over his rookie campaign.

Projected Statline: 237 attempts, 864 yards and 7 TD

2025 Leader: Harold Fannin (72 receptions, 731 yards, 6 TD)

This is the most interesting projection to make because the Browns have three legitimate candidates to lead the team in receiving.

Judkins might not be playing well, but there aren't really other options on the roster. Harold Fannin has a lot more competition as the incumbent leading receiver.

If we were handicapping the race, the tight end would have the third-best odds. That's a good thing for the Browns passing attack. The question is whether the passing game is going to evolve over the season.

Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have emerged as legitimate reasons for optimism in Cleveland. Concepcion has caught 10 of his 11 targets for 71 yards. Boston has turned his 11 targets into seven receptions for 154 yards and two touchdowns.

Boston has to be considered the favorite to lead the team in receiving yards. He's the team's best big-play threat at this point and he holds an 83-yard advantage already.

Concepcion should be considered a real threat to lead the team as well, though. His role in the offense gives him easy touches and the potential to rack up yards after the catch.

Regardless of how the quarterback plays on a weekly basis, they are going to be able to get Concepcion the ball on screens, jet sweeps and quick game. That should open the door for him to consistently produce.

Still, Boston's hot start makes it hard to pick against him.

Projected Statline: 62 receptions, 1,023 yards, 6 TD

2025 Leader: Myles Garrett (23 sacks, 33 TFL, 39 Quarterback Hits)

This is obviously where the biggest drop off is going to happen. Myles Garrett had one of the best pass-rushing seasons in the history of the league last season. Now, he's a Los Angeles Ram and the Browns are searching for a primary pass rusher.

Thus far, it looks like second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham the leader of the pass-rushers. Graham has already posted two sacks in two games after notching just half a sack during the entire 2025 season.

Graham is not Garrett. He is off to a hot start, though. He didn't just luck into two sacks, he is winning 18 percent of his pass-rush reps, per ESPN Analytics .

That puts him 14th among all interior defenders in the league through two weeks, but that number would have made him No. 2 among all defensive tackles last year.

That would put him somewhere around Jeffery Simmons who had 11 sacks last season. Offensive lines are bound to adjust to him as the season goes and Graham has more film to analyze.

The breakout trajectory combined with the fact that the other two sacks for the Browns have come from safeties Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman make Graham the obvious choice to lead the team in sacks.

Projected Statline: 8 sacks, 13 TFL, 15 Quarterback Hits

2025 Leader: 156 tackles (67 solo, 89 assists), 11 TFL, 2.5 sacks, 2 INT

Carson Schwesinger introduced himself to the league as a rookie by leading the 2025 Cleveland Browns in tackles. He was also named the AP Defensive Rookie of the Year.

Through two games, he's declared himself as the odds-on favorite to be the most producive linebacker on the team once more. He has posted 10 total tackles in each of the first two games.

Schwesinger is all over the field and is a clutch contributor for the defense. He reached a max speed of 20.56 MPH when tracking down Bucky Irving in the opend field and he took down Baker Mayfield on a crucial third-down scramble.

Graham is shaping up to be the kind of interior pass rusher who can take over a game. Schwesinger is showing he can be the down-to-down leader who will make more splash plays as he uses the experience he gained last year.

We could be looking at an All-Pro season.

Projected Statline: 162 tackles (89 solo), 13 TFL, 3 sacks, 2 INT

articles.title: Buying and Selling Playoff Chances of the NFL's 2-0 and 0-2 Teams Entering Week 3
articles.summary: After two games, half the NFL is either in the penthouse or the outhouse. Rolling and undefeated or reeling and winless.
articles.body:
After two games, half the NFL is either in the penthouse or the outhouse. Rolling and undefeated or reeling and winless.

Now, a 2-0 start doesn't guarantee anything—since the postseason expanded to 14 teams in 2020, one in four teams that start the season 2-0 miss the playoffs altogether. Conversely, an 0-2 start isn't the kiss of death. In each of the past two seasons, three teams that started the season 0-2 made the playoffs. Three teams that have started the season with back-to-back losses won the Super Bowl—the 1993 Cowboys, 2001 Patriots and 2007 Giants.

In other words, at least one of this year's hot starters will probably falter and wind up watching the playoffs from home. And there's a real chance that one of those slow starters will shake it off and get into the postseason tournament.

Here's a look at the chances each actually happens.

The Buffalo Bills are the easiest call on this list. And team for whom just making the playoffs would be viewed s a massive disappointment. It's Super Bowl or bust in Western New York this year.

We're just two games into the Joe Brady era, but based on early returns the Bills look like the class of the AFC, Only the Kansas City Chiefs are averaging more yards per game. The Bills are averaging a ridiculous 38.5 points per game. Quarterback Josh Allen looks like the early front-runner for MVP.

There is a potential problem looming though—the Bills are 28th in total defense and 30th against the pass.

That could be a problem in the postseason. But right now, it's just about impossible to imagine Buffalo not getting there.

This is something of a make-or-break season for Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals.

So far, the Bengals are doing a lot more making than breaking.

The Cincinnati offense is choked with talent. Burrow. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Running back Chase Brown. But so far this season, it's the team's new-look defense that has been the story.

Last week against the Houston Texans, the Bengals gave up yards aplenty—374 to be precise. What they didn't give up is points—when the Texans got close, the Bengals stiffened, and Houston finished the game with just six points.

If the Cincinnati defense plays at anywhere near the level we have seen from the offense in recent years, this team could do more than just make the postseason.

The Bengals can make it all the way to Los Angeles and Super Bowl LXI.

Last year, 10 teams started the season 0-2. Three of those teams went on to make the postseason—the Carolina Panthers, the Chicago Bears—and the Houston Texans. It marked the second time in the last three years that Houston started the season with consecutive losses but made the playoffs.

Apparently the Texans like to make things interesting.

Houston is moving the ball—the Texans are ninth in the NFL in total offense. But the team isn't finishing drives, and a defense that was expected to be among the league's best is off to a slow start.

The Texans need to be more efficient on offense. The offensive line has to get better. And the Houston defense needs to get untracked.

But playing in a division where only one team has a win, it's too early to count the Texans out.

When the Indianapolis Colts hit the bye week last year, the team was 8-2 and one of the NFL's biggest surprises.

The Colts haven't won a regular season game since—last week's overtime loss in Kansas City was Indy's ninth in a row.

The team at least showed some signs of life at Arrowhead after getting blasted by the ravens in Week 1, but there are major problems on both sides of the ball. No. 1 wide receiver Alec Pierce is out indefinitely with a foot injury. Someone forgot to tell the defense that the season started—the Colts have allowed 74 points in two games.

Playing in a soft AFC South helps, but the Colts have shown little so far to indicate that a big-time rebound is in the offing.

After last year's 6-11 faceplant, the Kansas City Chiefs entered the 2026 season under a cloud of uncertainty—something that has been exceedingly rare over the past decade-plus.

If the first two weeks of the season are any indication, that uncertainty was unwarranted—and the Chiefs are "back."

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is showing no ill effects from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 campaign. Tight end Travis Kelce looks closer to 27 than 37. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been a revelation in his first year with the team.

The Chiefs admittedly play in arguably the NFL's toughest division. But Kansas City is first in the NFL in total offense. Second in total defense. And as battle-tested as any team in the NFL.

There isn't a more surprising undefeated team in the NFL right now than the Las Vegas Raiders. Beating the hapless Dolphins in the opener was one thing. Knocking off the Chargers in Los Angeles last week is another.

This was supposed to be a team in the opening stages of a rebuild breaking in a rookie quarterback. Instead, veteran stopgap Kirk Cousins has three touchdown passes in each of his first two starts. Running back Ashton Jeanty is averaging over 100 total yards per game. And a defense that was overhauled in the offseason is allowing less than 14 points per game.

Will this success be sustainable? Probably not—the schedule is about to get a lot more daunting.

But for a long-suffering fanbase starved for success, this hot start has to feel good.

The Los Angeles Chargers were supposed to be contenders in the AFC West this year.

Instead, two weeks into the season the Chargers are cooked.

It's not just that the Bolts lost their first two games. It's that the Chargers lost both games at home by double-digits to a pair of teams that picked in the top-three of April's draft. Tomato cans.

An offense that was supposed to take off under new coordinator Mike McDaniel crashed on the runway. The defense has regressed with Jesse Minter gone. The Chargers are turning the ball over. Committing far too many penalties. Quarterback Justin Herbert is playing the worst football of his career.

Simply put, the Chargers are a mess. And with a brutal stretch on the schedule starting this week in Buffalo, the Chargers might as well get comfortable in the AFC West cellar.

Credit where it's due. When the Miami Dolphins decide they want to be bad, they don't mess around.

It was hardly a state secret that the Dolphins were going to struggle after an offseason roster purge. The offense has no passing-game weapons. The defense is a who's who of "who?"

But the Dolphins have exceeded suckspectations. Two weeks in, Miami is 27th in total offense, 30th in scoring offense and 30th in scoring defense. The Dolphins hve been outscored 62-26 and have been competitive for about five minutes.

It's not like there's something that can be pointed to as a potential springboard back to respectability, either. The Dolphins are the most talent-deficient team in the league.

From all indications that was by design. The Dolphins have hit the rest button and are looking ahead to 2027.

That's going to make 2026 hard to watch.

Of the NFL's undefeated teams, the Minnesota Vikings are the most difficult to get a read on.

To their credit, the Vikings have shown resilience in coming back at home against the Green Bay Packers and winning on the road in terrible weather against the Chicago Bears. Brian Flores' defense has been aggressive and tenacious, ranking fourth in the league in points allowed.

But there are questions on offense. Can quarterback Kyler Murray keep up the momentum that Carson Wentz built after Murray suffered a concussion early in that Week 1 win over the Pack? Can a backfield that has been hit hard by injuries hold up?

It's far too early to anoint the Vikings a Super Bowl contender. Or even the class of the NFC North. But back-to-back division wins over 2025 playoff teams can't be ignored, and Minnesota's defense is going to keep them in a lot of games.

When the season began, it appeared that the NFC East was going to be a lot more competitive than it was in 2025.

Two weeks in, it will be a huge upset if the Philadelphia Eagles don't win the division for the fourth time in the last five seasons. The Dallas Cowboys can't play defense—again. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders both watched their starting quarterback go down with a major injury last week.

It's not that the Eagles don't have issues of their own. The offense has been inconsistent to this point in the season. An Eagles pass rush that is perennially among the NFL's best has struggled to generate pressure, with just three sacks over the season's first two games.

Still, the Eagles have a much better defense than the Cowboys, and the Commanders and Giants are toast.

The argument can be made that no team in the NFL has looked more impressive over the first two weeks of the season. After rolling the rival Rams in Australia, the 49ers blasted the Miami Dolphins. The Niners have outscored their two opponents 62-20.

Brock Purdy is playing as well as any quarterback in the game—he's completing over 80 percent of his passes and has five touchdown passes against just one interception. The San Francisco defense is 10th in yards allowed and third in points allowed.

The schedule moving forward is favorable—four of San Francisco's next six opponents missed the playoffs in 2025. If San Francisco can take down the Seahawks in Seattle in Week 5, they can take control of the NFC West.

Injuries seemingly constantly loom over the 49ers. But that's the only thing that could keep this team out of the postseason.

When the Seattle Seahawks lost quarterback Sam Darnold just a handful of snaps into the season-opener, it looked like the defending champs might be in trouble.

Seattle squeaked past the New England Patriots in a defensive battle in Week 1 before blasting the Arizona Cardinals last week. Their recipe for success has been similar to last year—a healthy dose of the run game, the heroics of wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and one of the best defenses in the game.

Darnold could play this week against the reeling Commanders, but even if he sits Drew Lock has shown he can hold down the fort until Darnold's back. With the winless Chargers coming after that, Seattle will likely be undefeated when the 49ers come to visit for an important early showdown in Week 5.

When the Tampa Bay Buccaneers gave Baker Mayfield an extension averaging $55 million a season, this wasn't what they had in mind.

After losing to the Cleveland Browns at home last week, the Buccaneers have dropped nine of their last 11 regular season games. Not much is working for the team right now—Mayfield is averaging less than 200 passing yards a game and has just one touchdown pass, and the Buccaneers defense sits 26th in the league in points allowed.

With that said, it's not a huge stretch to say that the Buccaneers are better than how they have looked so far this year, and it only took eight wins to capture the NFC South last year.

The Buccaneers aren't dead. But if Tampa falls at home to the Vikings this week, the team is going to be in serious trouble.

When the Tennessee Titans hired Robert Saleh as head coach, he was supposed to make a team that is 6-28 the past two years more competitive.

Granted, the Titans gave the Philadelphia Eagles a game last week. But the result was all too familiar—another defeat. The Titans defense has allowed 354 yards per game—ninth-most in the league. The Tennessee offense is atrocious once again—no team in the AFC has amassed fewer yards per game. The Titans are rushing for just 95 yards per game and are 30th in passing.

It's that offense that is the real problem. Quarterback Cam Ward has shown little development since being drafted first overall, and while Titans have some passing-game weapons they are of little use if the quarterback can't get them the ball.

The Titans are the worst team in a bad division. And they aren't going anywhere.

With each passing week, it looks more and more likely the Washington Commanders' run to the NFC Championship Game in 2024 was a fluke—and less and less likely that the team will get anywhere near that contest any time soon.

The biggest reason for that is glaringly obvious—quarterback Jayden Daniels can't stay on the field. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year dislocated his elbow (again) in last week's lopsided loss to the Dallas Cowboys. And when Daniels suffered a similar injury last season, he took the entire Commanders offense with him.

The defense isn't helping matters either. Last year, Washington fielded the league's worst defense in terms of yards allowed. This year, the Commanders are one of six teams surrendering over 30 points per game.

articles.title: Tucker Kraft Calls Out Packers Fans for Booing During Loss to Falcons, 'Not Going to Help Us Win'
articles.summary: Frustration is already mounting for the Green Bay Packers and their fans, who showered the team with boos for their performance during Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
Frustration is already mounting for the Green Bay Packers and their fans, who showered the team with boos for their performance during Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field.

Packers tight end Tucker Kraft criticized the home crowd for their response after the game, telling reporters that reaction is "not going to help us win" as they look for solutions amid a 1-2 start to the season:

"That's pretty tough. Like everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos. I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing, especially for a home opener. It's pretty disappointing. It's not going to help us win. Like I don't know what people think that's going to rally us or something like that. But that's — we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. But it'd probably much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us."

It's hard to know what else Packers fans were supposed to do during the game. Their team did start well with Christian Watson catching a four-yard touchdown pass late in the first quarter to give Green Bay a 7-0 lead.

Unfortunately, that was the Packers' peak. The Falcons scored 27 unanswered points to take a 27-7 lead early in the fourth quarter.

The 35 points for Atlanta on Thursday night more than doubled its total from the first two games combined (16). The Falcons had five red-zone trips against Green Bay, scoring touchdowns on four of them. They did not get into the red zone the first two weeks of the season.

Bijan Robinson ran all over the Packers defense with 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries. He had two runs of at least 30 yards, while the entire Packers team had a total of 17 rushing yards on nine carries.

This was the first time the Packers have lost a home opener since the 2012 season. The 21-point margin of defeat was the worst home loss of Matt LaFleur's tenure as head coach.

When you start adding all of that up, the Packers are not playing functional football. It's not a surprise watching the product on the field that fans would get restless and make their thoughts known.

The Packers will look to right the ship next week when they travel to Raymond James Stadium to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

articles.title: Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri, 53, who retired as the NFL's all-time leader with 599 field goals, made a 33-yard kick on snow at 11,317 feet in the Swiss Alps to set a Guinness record for the highest field goal
articles.summary: Adam Vinatieri has never needed a normal setting to make a memorable kick.
articles.body: Adam Vinatieri has never needed a normal setting to make a memorable kick. More than six years after his final NFL appearance, the Pro Football Hall of Famer found himself standing on snow in the Swiss Alps, thousands of feet above sea level, with the wind moving around him. Then came the familiar routine. A short run-up, clean contact and the ball sailing between the uprights. At 53, Vinatieri had found another way to make football history.Adam Vinatieri makes history at 11,332 feetOn September 22, Vinatieri travelled to Jungfraujoch in Switzerland, a mountain destination widely known as the “Top of Europe.” There, at an altitude of 3,454 metres, or about 11,332 feet above sea level, he successfully converted a 33-yard field goal and earned recognition for the highest-altitude American football field goal. The attempt took place on snow-covered ground, with wind adding another layer of difficulty to a kick that already had little in common with a normal NFL field goal.The location alone made the attempt unusual. NFL kickers are accustomed to pressure, hostile crowds, changing weather and difficult field conditions. Vinatieri had experienced all of those throughout a career that lasted 24 seasons. But Jungfraujoch presented a different challenge.At that elevation, the environment changes the experience of even a simple movement. The air is thinner, breathing becomes harder and the body responds differently to exertion. Snow also changes the feel beneath the kicking foot, while swirling wind can affect both balance and the flight of the ball.Vinatieri did not have the comfort of a familiar stadium or a carefully prepared NFL field. Instead, he had the mountains around him and a small group of spectators watching as he attempted a kick that had never been made under those conditions before.After the ball went through the uprights, Guinness World Records recognised the achievement. A Guinness adjudicator was present for the attempt, according to reports surrounding the event.Vinatieri explains what made the kick differentFor Vinatieri, the most striking part of the experience was not the snow. Snow had been part of his football story for decades.He became famous for delivering some of the most important kicks in New England Patriots history, including his unforgettable field goal against the Oakland Raiders in the 2001 AFC divisional playoff game. That kick came through heavy snow and helped New England survive a dramatic postseason contest before the team went on to win its first Super Bowl.So when Vinatieri returned to snowy conditions for the Guinness attempt, there was an obvious connection to his past. Yet he made it clear that the Swiss Alps offered a challenge unlike anything he had experienced during his NFL career.“Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots,” said Vinatieri, who converted plenty of kicks in snowy conditions during his career, including in the 2001 season’s AFC Championship Game against the Raiders. “But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever done. You feel the altitude with every breath you take, your heart rate is different, your rhythm is different, and no one can really tell you beforehand how it will affect the kick, because no one has done this before. The fact that we were able to set the record under these conditions makes me very proud.”That comment captures why the record was more than a ceremonial kick. Vinatieri was dealing with variables that could not simply be recreated in a training session. His breathing, timing and rhythm all had to adjust to an environment far removed from an NFL stadium.He also had to trust a technique he had refined over decades. That may have been the most familiar part of the entire experience.Adam Vinatieri’s Patriots legacy adds another layerThe choice of Vinatieri for the record attempt was hardly random. His career is closely tied to difficult kicks in difficult moments, particularly during his years with the Patriots.Vinatieri spent 10 seasons in New England before playing 14 seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. He finished his NFL career with four Super Bowl victories, three Pro Bowl selections and more than 2,600 points. He retired after the 2019 season as the league's all-time leader in field goals made, with 599.His biggest moments often came when the margin for error was tiny.In Super Bowl XXXVI, Vinatieri made the game-winning field goal against the St. Louis Rams as time expired. Two years later, he again delivered the deciding kick in Super Bowl XXXVIII, this time against the Carolina Panthers. His snow-covered kick against the Raiders remains another defining image from the early Patriots dynasty.That history made the setting in Switzerland feel almost symbolic. Vinatieri once again had snow beneath his feet and a football in front of him. The difference was that instead of fighting for a Super Bowl, he was attempting to add a Guinness World Records title to a career that had already earned a place in Canton.Vinatieri was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 2026, making the record attempt an especially timely addition to his post-playing career.The record attempt connects to the Patriots’ Munich gameThe Swiss Alps kick also had a purpose beyond celebrating Vinatieri's career. The New England Patriots staged the event as part of the build-up to their upcoming international game against the Detroit Lions in Munich on November 15.That connection helped give the event a distinctly Patriots feel. Vinatieri wore a Patriots jersey during the attempt, bringing one of the franchise's most recognisable figures back into the spotlight.The location was also significant. The Patriots have a strong connection with Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and the franchise has been using the region as part of its international outreach. The Munich game will give the team another chance to connect with European NFL fans.For Vinatieri, however, the story remained much simpler. He was back in the snow, preparing for one more kick.There was no playoff clock. No Super Bowl trophy waiting at the other end. No packed NFL stadium demanding perfection.Instead, there was a mountain, a set of goalposts and a football.Then there was Vinatieri.The former kicker split the uprights and walked away with another piece of history. His latest achievement does not change his NFL statistics or add another championship to his résumé. It does something different. It shows that even after retirement, Vinatieri can still find a new challenge that feels worthy of the reputation he built over a remarkable career.From snowy playoff fields in New England to a mountain peak in Switzerland, the setting changed completely. The expectation did not.Make the kick. articles.title: Travis Kelce is reportedly planning a $20 million career reinvention that could redefine what it means to be a retired NFL superstar in modern America
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is two games into what could be his final NFL season, and already the conversation is shifting.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is two games into what could be his final NFL season, and already the conversation is shifting. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end, 36, signed a one-year, $12 million deal this offseason after flirting with retirement, and while he has delivered on the field, the bigger question isn't about football anymore. ESPN host and Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman believes he knows exactly where Kelce is headed once the cleats come off, and it involves a broadcasting payday that could reach $20 million a year.What broadcasting career is Travis Kelce predicted to pursue after retiring from the NFL?Aikman made his prediction during an appearance on the Sports Media with Richard Deitsch podcast, drawing from a one-on-one conversation with Kelce ahead of the Chiefs' Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos. His read on the situation was direct. "It sounds like he wants to do television," Aikman said. "I can't imagine that he won't. And I think there's going to be a line-up of suitors for his talents, and then it's just a matter of what exactly does he want that to look like."Aikman didn't stop there. He flagged the real question that every network executive will eventually face: does Travis Kelce want to call games from the booth, anchor a studio show, or carve out a more flexible arrangement that lets him travel with wife Taylor Swift? "Does he maybe want to have a limited schedule where he can still travel and watch his wife perform from time to time?" Aikman said.The Athletic's Andrew Marchand had already placed the financial stakes on the table earlier this year, projecting Kelce could command anywhere from $10 million to $20 million annually as a broadcaster. That kind of number isn't outlandish given the market. The landscape has changed dramatically since Aikman himself made the leap from playing to broadcasting in the early 2000s. Back then, a retired athlete landing a prime television role was unusual. Now it's a full-blown bidding war, and Kelce arrives with something most candidates don't, a mainstream profile that stretches far beyond sports.How much is Travis Kelce's 'New Heights' podcast earning, and does it affect his TV future?Before any network writes that check, there's a more immediate question about Travis Kelce's media footprint. His podcast with brother Jason Kelce, New Heights, ranked No. 7 on Forbes' list of highest-paid podcasters in 2026, pulling in $35 million between June 2025 and June 2026. That's serious independent income, the kind that gives Kelce real leverage in any negotiation.Jason Kelce's path offers a useful reference point. After retiring from the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, Jason signed a three-year, $24 million deal with ESPN, even while New Heights was already thriving. The podcast didn't block the TV move. It may have made it more attractive. Travis Kelce's situation mirrors that trajectory, except his celebrity profile is exponentially larger, his marriage to Swift has turned him into a household name well outside of NFL circles, and the networks know it.Aikman, who attended the Kelce-Swift wedding at Madison Square Garden in July, summed it up plainly. "The sky's the limit for him," he said.That's not just flattery. Kelce is already juggling brand partnerships with Sleep Number and Six Flags, a Tommy Hilfiger campaign, film roles, and television appearances. articles.title: Tucker Kraft on Packers fans booing: 'It's not gonna help us win'
articles.summary: The Packers were booed off Lambeau Field during their Thursday night loss to the Falcons.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers dropped to 1-2 on the season after a 35-14 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons on "Thursday Night Football." It wasn't the best home opener and the crowd at Lambeau Field let the players know by serenading them with boos during the game.

Many of the Packers players understood the frustration from the fans and understood they as a team did not do anything to change the mood inside the stadium.

Tight end Tucker Kraft , who caught four passes for 26 yards, said hearing the boos was "pretty disappointing" and didn't understand the crowd turning on the home side.

"That's pretty tough," Kraft said via ESPN's Matt Schneidman . "Everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos when I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing. Especially for a home opener. It's pretty disappointing. It's not gonna help us win. I don't know what people think, that's gonna rally us or something like that. But we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. But it'd probably be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us."

The lone victory through three games is the worst start the Packers have had under head coach Matt LaFleur in eight seasons. The offensive line is banged up. The running game, which totaled 17 yards against the Falcons, was nonexistent. And the Packers had the ball for 15 fewer minutes in the game than the Falcons.

LaFleur, whose seat is heating up , was at a loss afterward, saying, "I don't know what we're doing well offensively."

Kraft added they're only three games into the season and there's a lot of football left to be played.

"We can't let external noise divide us," Kraft said. "Us guys in this locker room, we're really all we've got. We spend a lot of time together, so just continue to stay close and build off each other."

The Packers will return to action in Week 4 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before welcoming the Chicago Bears and the Dallas Cowboys to Lambeau Field.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury Update, New Timeline Revealed by Commanders GM After Elbow Dislocation
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is going to avoid a stint injured reserve as he recovers from a dislocated elbow suffered in a Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is going to avoid a stint injured reserve as he recovers from a dislocated elbow suffered in a Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Commanders general manager Adam Peters told reporters on Friday that Daniels doesn't need surgery "as of right now" and there have been no discussions about putting him on IR.

An IR stint would keep Daniels out for a minimum of four games, so the Commanders appear hopeful he can return sooner than later.

Daniels, 25, has been beset by injuries during his NFL career, having missed 10 games with elbow, knee and hamstring injuries in 2025.

When healthy, he's emerged as one of the most dynamic playmakers in football, throwing for 5,090 yards, 36 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 26 career games while adding 1,269 yards and eight touchdowns on the ground. The Commanders are 14-12 in his starts.

Marcus Mariota will get the start on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks and will be under center for the foreseeable future until Daniels is ready to return.

"When you ask anybody on our team who some of our greatest leaders are, whether it's on or off the field, Marcus is somebody that constantly comes up," head coach Dan Quinn told reporters after Daniels suffered dislocated his elbow on Sept. 20.

"Marcus is a complete pro and has been that way since he's been here," veteran wideout Terry McLaurin added . "He's one of the leaders we look to. In the time he and I have been together, we've had success. We're going to rally around him."

But the Commanders are simply a different team with Daniels under center. Any chance they have of truly contending starts and ends with No. 5.

Mariota fared well taking over for Daniels against the Cowboys. He finished 11-of-16 for 111 yards and one touchdown in a 37-20 loss.

Washington's next four games are against the Seahawks, Indianapolis Colts, New York Giants and San Francisco 49ers before a Week 7 bye.

Johnson has logged four receptions, 14 total touches, and 103 scrimmage yards this season.

While Johnson will remain a matchup-based flex play for the foreseeable future, he has a terrific matchup this week. The Chiefs will visit the Miami Dolphins, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs.

There's also a very good chance that the Chiefs will get up big on the Dolphins early and look to grind out the game on the ground. In that scenario, Johnson should see a sizeable workload. He's rostered in 26 percent of leagues.

Dontayvion Wicks, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

Following the Philadelphia Eagles' trade of A.J. Brown, most expected rookie Makai Lemon to quickly emerge as the team's No. 2 receiver behind DeVonta Smith. However, it's been trade acquisition Dontayvion Wicks in that role thus far.

Wicks ranks second on the team with seven catches and 147 receiving yards. He's also tied for second with one touchdown. He's seen no fewer than four targets in a game, and his role could grow with tight end Dallas Goedert battling an MCL sprain.

This week, Wicks probably doesn't have the highest ceiling, as the Chicago Bears are expected to be without their top two quarterbacks. If Chicago struggles to keep pace on the scoreboard, Jalen Hurts is unlikely to spend the game in pass-first mode. However, Wicks' floor as a flex option is solid, and he has a good amount of long-term upside.

Wicks is rostered in 32 percent of fantasy leagues.

Oronde Gadsden II, TE, Los Angeles Chargers

The Los Angeles Chargers' offense hasn't been very good in 2026, and it appears that Justin Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel are still trying to mesh. However, managers looking for a tight end should still consider Oronde Gadsden II.

Gadsden is likely to leap into a significant role for L.A. after the Chargers placed David Njoku on injured reserve. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar is also dealing with a forearm injury.

While Gadsden has just four catches for 50 yards this season, he did find the end zone in Week 2, and he should see plenty of targets against the Buffalo Bills this week. Buffalo has looked like one of the league's top teams through two weeks, and the Chargers may have to pass often to keep pace.

Buffalo has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends in 2026. Gadsden is rostered in 25 percent of leagues.

articles.title: Drake London Calls Michael Penix Jr. 'Definition of Resiliency' After Falcons' Upset of Packers
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. received high praise from Drake London after leading the Atlanta Falcons to an impressive 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers for their first victory of the season.
articles.body:
Michael Penix Jr. received high praise from Drake London after leading the Atlanta Falcons to an impressive 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers for their first victory of the season.

London told reporters after the game that Penix is the "definition of resiliency" as the third-year quarterback worked his way back from a torn ACL in his left knee.

Making his first start since Week 11 of the 2025 season, Penix had some rust coming out of the gate with an interception that ended Atlanta's first offensive possession.

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

Penix settled in after that to finish 18-of-25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception. He helped the Falcons record season-highs in points, passing yards and total yards (498).

Even though there was no real question that Penix would return after injuring his knee last season, concerns about his viability only grew since it was the third time has torn his ACL.

The previous two times occurred in college and were to the ACL in his right knee, but there isn't a long history of NFL players returning and having success after having at least three ACL tears.

Former Carolina Panthers linebacker Thomas Davis Sr. is the most famous example of being able to do it. He tore the same ACL in three consecutive seasons from 2009 to '11 before returning to play nine additional seasons from 2012 to '20.

Penix's health and success is a huge storyline for the Falcons in 2026. He was a first-round pick two years ago and will become eligible for a contract extension after this season.

If Penix performs well, it will remove a huge question for Atlanta's front office to answer in the offseason as it looks to build up the roster.

There is a long way to go before getting to that point. Penix and the Falcons are currently focused on trying to play their way back into contention in what looks like a wide-open NFC South.

Next week is a marquee divisional showdown for the Falcons against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome on Monday Night Football.

articles.title: Jets Hit the NFL Draft Jackpot After Devastating Packers Loss
articles.summary: The New York Jets have hit the 2027 NFL Draft jackpot after the Green Bay Packers' devastating loss to start Week 3. The post Jets Hit the NFL Draft Jackpot...
articles.body:
New York Jets fans probably still have a bitter taste in their mouths after letting one slip away in Week 2. Well, here's the antidote to your problems: the Green Bay Packers just lost 35-14 to the Atlanta Falcons to start Week 3.

"The Cowboys– Micah Parsons trade was an incredible deal from a surplus value standpoint by Jerry Jones. Unfortunately for Cowboys fans, the later Quinnen Williams trade had a horrible condition that will give a potential top 5 overall Packers 2027 first rounder away," Super Bowl-winning NFL Coach and Director of Analytics Ryan Paganetti posted on X.

Wait a second, who controls the Packers' first-rounder in the 2027 NFL Draft? Oh, that's right, that would be the Jets.

General manager Darren Mougey pulled off a masterclass move by negotiating a clause into the Quinnen Williams blockbuster trade to the Dallas Cowboys . The Jets will get whichever pick is better in the first round between the Cowboys and the Packers.

According to Tankathon , that would be the Packers selection, with the team dropping to 1-2. If the draft started today, they would have the 8th overall pick, which would be sent to the Jets.

When the Jets put that clause into the trade at the deadline last year, it didn't create many waves around the league because of the teams involved.

The Packers and the Cowboys are iconic NFL franchises that don't end up at the top of the draft very often.

Since 2006, the lowest win total the Packers have put up is six wins. They did that twice: 2008 and 2018. Since 2003, the lowest win total the Cowboys have put up is four wins. It happened once during an injury-riddled 2015 season.

However, that's why the moniker says any given Sunday. The NFL is a funny sport. Who knows which teams will be good and which teams will be bad on a year-to-year basis.

Mougey hit the jackpot with this trade. The Packers are 1-2; they should really be 0-3, but we don't have to get into that. Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur was asked after the latest loss to start Week 3 if he's considering firing coaches on his staff, and he refused to answer the question.

Things are going badly, and it could only get worse from here. According to ESPN , the Packers currently have the 8th easiest strength of schedule, yet they are 1-2. The games are only going to get tougher from here, which should be great news for the green and white.

Gang Green will only get one pick from either the Packers or the Cowboys. If the draft started today, they would get Green Bay's pick. They also hold their own first-rounder in 2027, but wait, there's more.

In the blockbuster Sauce Gardner trade, the Jets secured the Colts' first-rounder in the 2027 NFL Draft as well.

If the draft started today, the Jets would land the No. 3 overall pick because of the Colts ' 0-2 start to the season, per Tankathon .

"After the Indianapolis Colts' overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, cornerback Sauce Gardner has not tasted victory on American soil in nearly two years. Gardner hasn't been on the winning side in the United States since a Dec. 2024 victory with the New York Jets, extending his personal losing streak to a whopping 644 days. During that span, his only winning experience was a victory by the Colts in the 2025 Berlin Game," Doric Sam of Bleacher Report wrote.

"Gardner endured a 0-7 start to the 2025 season with the Jets and sat out their first win in Week 8 against the Cincinnati Bengals . He was sent to the Colts at the Nov. 4 trade deadline, and his new team ended the year on a seven-game losing streak after defeating the Atlanta Falcons in Germany," Sam revealed.

The Jets have two big horses in the 2027 NFL Draft. Draft expert Trevor Sikkema told me on "Boy Green Daily" before the season that this 2027 class has a chance to be one of the best in a long time. That should be music to Jets fans' ears everywhere.

articles.title: Packers’ Week 3 blowout loss to Falcons has 2x Super Bowl champ ringing alarm bells
articles.summary: Damien Woody warns the Packers face serious issues.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers suffered another heavy defeat Thursday, losing 35-14 to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field.

The loss dropped Green Bay to 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Atlanta also improved to 1-2 after controlling the game from the second quarter.

Damien Woody, who won two Super Bowl championships as an offensive lineman with the New England Patriots , thinks the Packers have serious problems across both sides of the line. Speaking on the NFL on CBS broadcast, he delivered a blunt assessment.

"They're in trouble," Woody said, per NFL on CBS on X . "Oh, the Green Bay Packers are in trouble."

Woody pointed directly at Green Bay's inability to establish the line of scrimmage. The Packers finished with only 17 rushing yards on nine carries.

"First of all, up front, they can't run the football," Woody said. "That's the most evident thing about the Green Bay Packers."

The lack of rushing production placed additional pressure on quarterback Jordan Love throughout the night. Atlanta eventually built enough pressure to disrupt Green Bay's offensive rhythm.

"The Green Bay Packers are in TROUBLE!" 😳 @damienwoody #Final pic.twitter.com/YbJHIGaIGB — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 25, 2026

"The Green Bay Packers are in TROUBLE!" 😳 @damienwoody #Final pic.twitter.com/YbJHIGaIGB

NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 25, 2026

The Packers also struggled to protect Love against an aggressive Falcons defense. Atlanta held the Packers to 328 total yards while producing 498 yards offensively.

"They can't protect the quarterback, and tonight, they got absolutely gashed by the Atlanta Falcons ' rushing attack," Woody said.

Packers face bigger questions after Atlanta collapse

Glendale, Arizona, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

NFL Network's Michael Robinson identified another issue involving Atlanta's defensive approach. He said defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's pressure looks appeared designed to speed up Love's decision-making.

"If you make Jordan Love think that he's going to get pressure, you're going to already speed up his process," Robinson said, per NFL Network on X . "Then you get the mistakes."

Atlanta rushed for 242 yards, with Bijan Robinson producing 194 yards and two touchdowns. Receiver Drake London added 194 yards as the Falcons repeatedly created explosive plays.

Robinson also questioned how Green Bay will function without Josh Jacobs, who remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The veteran running back's absence left the Packers without their primary rushing threat.

"This offense very badly needs a difference-maker at the running back position," Robinson said. "You can't have the play-action explosives if the guy behind you ain't there."

"This offense, very badly needs a difference maker at the running back position." — @RealMikeRob on his concern for the Packers after their loss to the Falcons. pic.twitter.com/ZmgsGh9eJa — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) September 25, 2026

"This offense, very badly needs a difference maker at the running back position." — @RealMikeRob on his concern for the Packers after their loss to the Falcons. pic.twitter.com/ZmgsGh9eJa

NFL Network (@nflnetwork) September 25, 2026

The Packers next face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road on Oct. 4. Green Bay must improve its rushing attack and protection before that matchup.

As Woody summarized, the problems extend beyond one position. "If you can't capture the line of scrimmage on either side of the ball, you're going to be in big trouble."

articles.title: NFL Exec Says 'Every Team' Looks for Edge with Social Media Videos After Mike Macdonald's Comments
articles.summary: Multiple NFL coaches and executives shrugged off Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's admitted use of social media videos in scouting, noting that it is commonplace in the league.
articles.body:
Multiple NFL coaches and executives shrugged off Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's admitted use of social media videos in scouting, noting that it is commonplace in the league.

Speaking to Jeff Howe of The Athletic, an anonymous high-ranking team executive called the situation a "nothing burger," adding, "Every team does it."

An anonymous coach agreed, saying, "It's very common. We all do it. Everyone does."

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

Meanwhile, an anonymous general manager called the controversy "absolutely nothing" and "a waste of time."

Earlier this week, a clip went public from Macdonald's appearance on In Depth With Graham Bensinger (h/t ESPN's Brady Henderson ), and in it, Macdonald admitted to using clips of training camp practices posted by fans on social media in order to scout the Denver Broncos prior to their 2024 regular-season opener.

"Fans will post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's like public knowledge," Macdonald said. "We took like 100 plays from their training camp. We were scouting them."

Macdonald noted that Broncos head coach Sean Payton was initially furious about the tactics after finding out about them, going so far as to contact Seahawks general manager John Schneider.

"He got wind of it and he lost it," Macdonald said. "This is the middle of the season, and we won the game. We were in the fight our first year. There was a lot of s--t going on. So, he called John. He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing.

"I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So, we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

One day after the story began making the rounds, Macdonald told reporters he apologized to Payton for it becoming public.

Payton then told reporters he has "a ton of respect for" Macdonald, adding, "He and I are good. Lord knows I've been in his position, you know, you're talking about something. The story is about three years ago."

Macdonald has enjoyed enormous success during his time as the Seahawks' head coach, posting a 26-10 record over parts of three seasons.

After narrowly missing the playoffs with a 10-7 record in his debut season, Macdonald led Seattle to a Super Bowl win last season.

The Seahawks are off to a 2-0 start early in the 2026 campaign, and they look like a threat to make another deep playoff run.

articles.title: NFL gameday: Brock Purdy 'in prime' for San Francisco 49ers, Patrick Mahomes chases Tom Brady record and Dexter Lawrence leads Cincinnati Bengals Super Bowl charge

articles.body:
He entered the league devoid of pressure or projections as Mr Irrelevant. Not long after he was tasked with leading perennial Super Bowl contention for the 49ers. Football onlookers have since been fiercely divided on where he stands among the NFL's premier quarterbacks. Was it the Kyle Shanahan system and the star-studded cast? Or is he just good? It is allowed to be both.

It comes with the asterisk of premature two-week conclusions territory, but Purdy is playing as well as any quarterback in football right now.

He enters week three with the highest completion percentage in the league at 80.4 having completed 45 of 56 passes for 492 yards and five touchdowns at 8.8 yards per attempt.

"We're starting to witness Brock's prime, and I think it's going to be a sight to behold," said 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams.

"I've always loved Brock, but I think he's starting to get his respect now. He doesn't even relish in it. It's all about next week, going 1-0, and that's why he's a great leader."

Purdy doesn't earn acclaim for being one of the league's most athletic or dynamic out-of-structure two-way killers, but instead thrives on high-level processing, field diagnosis, anticipation and accuracy. It should also be said he is a far better scrambler than he gets credit for.

The best of what Purdy represents came in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins on a precision-perfect strike to Mike Evans, the 49ers quarterback moving one defender with a pump-fake before sliding left and threading a stunning off-platform bullet to his new wide receiver. Evans had run what began as a crossing route before momentarily adjusting into a corner break, Purdy picking him out with expert touch and timing to execute on a flood concept.

Twice Purdy has threatened one of the great underdog stories in NFL history. He famously guided the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie after being selected with the 262nd and final pick of the Draft, only to suffer an elbow injury in the first quarter as Josh Johnson replaced him in a 31-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. He went one better the next season by taking San Francisco to Super Bowl LVIII, where they were beaten in overtime by the Kansas City Chiefs.

The system quarterback label has overshadowed him at times, while others have underlined his success in a scheme others have been unable to execute at such a high level. His 49ers have meanwhile been as unlucky with marquee injuries as any team in the league, as much hampering Shanahan's offense in recent years as they seek to work their way back to Super Bowl territory.

He now has a healthy Christian McCaffrey, a healthy George Kittle and, perhaps for the first time in his career, a proven elite veteran receiver in Mike Evans.

"I got really lucky," said Kittle on The Rich Eisen Show . "I get to play with Trent Williams right? We got him. Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still. Mike Evans, Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still.

"And so just when you add guys like that, it's just so much fun because every time we call a play and I know Mike has a chance of getting the ball, I'm like, 'this is so sick'. Brock Purdy's throwing the ball to Mike Evans and I'm blocking for him.

Purdy's 49ers look to go 3-0 this weekend when they take on the Arizona Cardinals, lead by one of Shanahan's disciples in first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.

The second-year corner out of Western Kentucky was showered with praise by Raheem Morris as San Francisco's 'player of the game on defense' against Miami, the 49ers defensive coordinator turning to the 24-year-old as an explosive blitz weapon capable of reading plays quickly, making stops laterally and adding another downhill threat to his defense.

articles.title: To kick or receive? NFL coaches still haven't figured out the overtime coin toss
articles.summary: The NFL changed overtime to guarantee both teams a possession, but that created a new strategic puzzle.
articles.body:
Prior to overtime last Sunday night, with his team in jeopardy of starting a pivotal season with two straight losses, Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen contemplated one of the toughest choices in football.

He had to decide whether to kick or receive if the Colts won the coin toss.

Winning the overtime coin toss used to be cause for celebration under the NFL's previous rules. The receiving team gained the opportunity to secure victory without its opponent touching the ball if it scored a touchdown on its opening possession.

The optimal strategy is far murkier now that the NFL's overtime system guarantees both teams possession of the ball. Winning the coin toss now means choosing between taking the ball first to chase a potential possession advantage or playing defense first to know exactly how many points are required to win.

The presence of quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the opposing huddle influenced Steichen's decision to give the Kansas City Chiefs the ball to start Sunday's overtime. As Steichen told reporters after the game, "If we go first with it, Mahomes gets four downs going the other way, so we wanted to play defense there and know we had four downs."

Steichen's decision backfired on the Colts when both teams settled for field goals on their initial possessions of overtime and Mahomes took advantage of getting the ball a second time. Harrison Butker's game-clinching 40-yard field goal sent the Chiefs spilling onto the field in celebration and sparked renewed debate over how teams should approach winning the overtime coin toss.

It's difficult to draw meaningful conclusions from the results of recent overtime games because the sample size is too small. Twenty games have gone to overtime since the NFL adopted the new rules for the playoffs in March 2022 and then extended them to the regular season in 2025. The team that won the overtime coin toss has chosen to kick in 14 of those 20 games. And yet the team that received the ball first is 11-8-1 (57.5%).

A study published by a football-obsessed cardiologist in The Journal of Sports Analytics this past July offered some of the first mathematical insight into the optimal strategy for the NFL's kick-or-receive overtime coin toss dilemma. Using a Monte Carlo simulation to predict which strategy would prove advantageous over 100,000 NFL overtimes, author Dylan Goings found that electing to receive the ball first would produce a win rate of 53.14%.

"Coaches who choose to kick are trading a structural positioning advantage for informational clarity that, in our analysis, does not translate to improved outcomes," Goings concluded.

Goings told Yahoo Sports he took on the project in his spare time last January after he and some college buddies got into a spirited debate over whether the Chicago Bears were right to kick the ball to the Rams at the start of overtime in the divisional playoffs. The cardiologist could not let the argument go unresolved, especially not when his background in medical research, risk stratification and statistical analysis gave him the tools to find a definitive answer.

"It's just the type of person I am," Goings said with a laugh. "If you have an argument with a friend and you have a hunch that you're right, let's settle it.

"I had already written code to do a Monte Carlo analysis for something very similar. So with just a few tweaks I had something that's relevant to football fans."

The key limitation to a Monte Carlo simulation — an analysis that uses random guessing over and over to predict the possible outcomes of an event — is that the results are only as good as the assumptions and probabilities that the researcher feeds into the simulation. Goings combatted that before submitting his study for publication by posting the results of his Monte Carlo simulation to a handful of Reddit forums and incorporating feedback on how heavily to weigh variables like two-point conversion strategy or clock pressure.

"It was like a peer review process from strangers on the internet," Goings said.

To test whether the optimal strategy varied if one team had an elite defense or a turnover-prone quarterback or a shaky kicker, Goings conducted a sensitivity analysis using extreme or even unrealistic efficiencies. There was no combination of variables, he said, where he found it was more advantageous to kick than to receive.

The best way for the team that has the ball second in overtime to eat into its disadvantage, according to Goings, is to aggressively go for the win on its initial possession. Whether by going for it on 4th-and-short instead of kicking a tying field goal or attempting a two-point conversion instead of kicking a tying extra point, those options are superior to matching scores and giving the opposing team possession of the ball in the sudden death format.

One of the most qualified people to assess Goings' findings might be a former backgammon world champion with a passion for game theory. Frank Frigo has worked with risk-averse NFL and college coaches to help them optimize their in-game decision making, first as a co-founder of data analysis firm EdjSports and now as an independent consultant.

When asked which strategy he favored for the overtime coin toss winner, Frigo told Yahoo Sports that he believes the potential to have a greater number of possessions by taking the ball first slightly outweighed the informational advantage of getting the ball second. Frigo hasn't run a full data simulation like Goings, but he pointed to data showing that 22.1% of NFL overtimes end on the third possession and 6.4% on the fifth.

"It's hard for me to imagine that the informational advantage of having the ball second outweighs that," Frigo said.

As fans in Buffalo know all too well, the NFL implemented its new overtime system in response to the Kansas City Chiefs beating the star-crossed Bills in the divisional round of the NFL playoffs in January 2022. After a thrilling, back-and-forth 60 minutes of regulation, the overtime coin flip had an outsize influence on the outcome. The Chiefs won the toss, and Mahomes promptly led them to a touchdown on the opening drive of overtime, stranding Josh Allen on the sideline with no way to respond, no way to impact the result.

The lack of debate over whether the kicking or receiving team has the advantage in overtime now is proof that the NFL's new system is working. Since the start of the 2025 regular season, the overtime coin toss winner has a record of 6-12-1. To this day, teams don't seem to fully understand how to capitalize on the slight structural advantage of receiving the ball first or how to negate much of the disadvantage of taking the ball second by playing for the win.

After his team lost 20-17 in overtime to the Green Bay Packers last Sunday, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn struggled to explain to reporters why he elected to receive the ball first in overtime. Glenn said the Jets were hoping to eat most of the 10-minute clock with their opening drive, score a touchdown and put pressure on the Packers to answer.

"It didn't happen for us the way that I planned," Glenn conceded.

To Goings, the most egregious overtime coin flip decision this season was his favorite team's. Having either not read Goings' study or not agreed with his conclusions, New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore — after winning the toss — chose to kick the ball to Detroit in a 31-30 week 1 overtime loss to the Lions.

"They did the exact opposite of the strategy I suggested," Goings lamented. "That was pretty frustrating to watch."
